classification.difficultyReason: Interpret three adjacent angles using square-grid geometry and inverse tangent ratios.

content.prompt: Explain how the diagram below shows that $\tan^{-1}(1)+\tan^{-1}(2)+\tan^{-1}(3)=180^{\circ}$.

spec.description: Two columns and three rows of equal square cells, with a triangle joining the top-left corner, the bottom-edge midpoint and the right-edge point two cells above the bottom. The populated grid requires TikZ because the blank-grid template cannot express the triangle and angle sectors.
spec.mathematics: Vertices (0,3), (1,0), (2,2). Three adjacent sectors at (1,0) partition the upper straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied grid, triangle and unlabelled coloured sectors are visible; angle values and reasoning remain in answers.

answer.short:
The orange, blue and red angles are $\tan^{-1}(3)$, $\tan^{-1}(1)$ and $\tan^{-1}(2)$ respectively.

They partition a straight angle, so their sum is $180^{\circ}$. The blue angle is $45^{\circ}$ because the triangle is isosceles and right-angled.
answer.worked:
Each grid square has unit side length. The orange angle has opposite side $3$ and adjacent side $1$; the red angle has opposite side $2$ and adjacent side $1$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan(\text{orange angle})&=\frac{3}{1}=3\\\text{orange angle}&=\tan^{-1}(3)\\\tan(\text{red angle})&=\frac{2}{1}=2\\\text{red angle}&=\tan^{-1}(2)\end{align*}$$

From the triangle's rightmost vertex, the other two vertices are reached by moving two squares left and one up, or one square left and two down. These equal displacement patterns differ by a quarter-turn, so the two sides are equal and perpendicular. The triangle is therefore isosceles and right-angled.

$$\begin{align*}\text{blue angle}&=\frac{180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}}{2}\\\text{blue angle}&=45^{\circ}=\tan^{-1}(1)\end{align*}$$

The three coloured angles form a straight angle. Hence
$$\tan^{-1}(1)+\tan^{-1}(2)+\tan^{-1}(3)=180^{\circ}.$$
